bug_semantics: Filter and Switch nodes compiled workflow-supplied regex patterns with new RegExp() and executed them synchronously on the worker thread with no complexity validation or execution timeout. A crafted pattern can catastrophic-backtrack per data item and stall other workflow executions on the same worker (CWE-1333 ReDoS).
flaw_origin: Original Switch-node feature. Commit 70728a00b7ae54c17fdd32b056f3c0dadae62947 first added packages/nodes-base/nodes/Switch.node.ts with a regex operator that parsed an optional /pattern/flags literal and otherwise compiled regex = new RegExp(value2.toString()), then ran value1.toString().match(regex) with no timeout. Later Filter (cc9fe7b91ffc4ea72c25e1242e0e477112cb283e), the shared filter-parameter helper (8a5343401dd355436120a9a424ae455e80b50da6), directory moves, and V1/V2 splits copied or relocated that same unsandboxed compile-and-match; they did not first write it.
evidence: First-party GHSA-q3fv-295f-qfpf (GitHub alias GHSA-jxf5-f3hg-vxvj) and CVE-2026-77082 describe ReDoS in Filter and Switch: user regex compiled with new RegExp() and executed synchronously without complexity validation or timeout. Bundle withdrawn_at is null; OSV lists the CVE as published 2026-08-20, CWE-1333, patched 1.123.69 / 2.33.4 / 2.34.1.
